intro: Start from the symptom that is present in the files, not from a guessed cause. Preserve the failed state, make the first discriminating check, and change one justified condition at a time.
boundary: This supporting index does not replace the A-E research workflow or software documentation. Program failure, solver convergence, observable convergence, physical validity, and a supported scientific claim remain separate questions.

sources.title: How to handle imaginary phonon modes
How to make an SCF run converge

records.title: The job stops before the calculation completes
records.symptom: The scheduler or launcher exits, the executable stops before its normal completion marker, or the output ends without a complete final electronic or ionic step.
records.first_check: Read the scheduler state, exit code, standard output, and standard error together. Determine whether the executable launched, whether it read the input, and which program stage completed last.
cause_classes: Launcher, module, shared-library, or MPI environment failure
Malformed, empty, or incorrectly redirected input
Wall-time, preemption, memory, disk, quota, or scratch failure
Application-level fatal error after execution began
inspect: Scheduler state, exit code, resource record, and job-level error stream
The first program banner and the last complete output block
Exact executable, version, launch command, input path, and scratch identity
Disk space, permissions, concurrent writers, and incomplete artifacts
safe_next_action: Correct only the demonstrated environment, resource, input, or storage fault.
If a diagnostic rerun is required, keep the scientific input unchanged and use isolated scratch with the smallest justified resource change.
preserve_before_retry: Input, job script, job ID, launch command, standard output, and standard error
Executable version, scheduler exit and resource record, and a hash or inventory of produced artifacts
records.do_not_conclude: A stopped job does not show that the SCF problem is scientifically unconverged, that the structure is unstable, or that a material property is absent. The run may have produced no usable DFT evidence.

records.title: The input, pseudopotential, or method is rejected
records.symptom: The program reports an input-reading error, unknown keyword, missing file, incompatible pseudopotential family, or inconsistent exchange-correlation setup.
records.first_check: Read the first fatal message against the input reference for the version that actually ran. Verify that the input is plain text and identify every pseudopotential or dataset exactly.
cause_classes: Syntax or keyword mismatch between the input and software version
Encoding, line-ending, path, permission, or empty-file problem
Incompatible exchange-correlation and pseudopotential or dataset choices
Invalid charge, spin, occupation, or boundary-condition specification
inspect: The exact rejected namelist, keyword, tag, and preceding error context
File type, line endings, paths, permissions, and referenced filenames
Pseudopotential metadata, exchange-correlation identity, valence configuration, and hashes
Charge, spin, occupation, and boundary-condition declarations
safe_next_action: Correct one evidenced input or compatibility fault at a time, using the documentation for the executed version.
Do not force an override merely to make the parser continue when it changes the declared method.
preserve_before_retry: The rejected input and complete error output
Executable version and exact pseudopotential or dataset identities and hashes
records.do_not_conclude: Successful parsing does not establish that the method is appropriate, that the numerical setup is converged, or that the resulting state is physically meaningful.

records.title: The electronic SCF cycle does not converge
records.symptom: The reported electronic residual does not reach its stopping condition, oscillates, rises after falling, or reaches the iteration limit.
records.first_check: Audit the structure, electron count, charge, spin state, occupations, band count, and residual history before changing the mixer or eigensolver.
cause_classes: Implausible geometry, charge, spin state, or initial density
Metallic occupation switching, too few empty states, or inadequate k-point sampling
Long-wavelength charge sloshing or unsuitable density mixing
Insufficient accuracy in the inner eigenproblem or an unsuitable solver
inspect: Residual and total-energy trends over every electronic iteration
Occupations, Fermi level, empty-state coverage, and k-point sampling
Magnetization or other state labels and whether they change during the cycle
Geometry, close contacts, warnings, and the exact stopping condition
safe_next_action: First correct the model, state, occupations, band coverage, or sampling problem that the output demonstrates.
Then test one documented mixer or eigensolver change in a bounded diagnostic run and return to the accepted numerical setup before interpreting a result.
preserve_before_retry: Complete input and output, including the full iteration history and warnings
Parent-state identity, restart ancestry, executable version, and hashes of reused artifacts
records.do_not_conclude: An SCF failure is not proof of physical instability. Conversely, a reported SCF convergence condition does not establish the lowest relevant state, observable convergence, model correctness, or a supported scientific claim.

records.title: The eigensolver, band count, or Fermi-level search fails
records.symptom: The output reports a diagonalization failure, unconverged eigenvectors, insufficient bands, or an inability to determine the Fermi level.
records.first_check: Verify geometry, electron count, pseudopotential or dataset identity, occupations, k-point sampling, broadening, and band count before switching algorithms.
cause_classes: Invalid structure, electron count, charge, or pseudopotential or dataset
Too few empty states or unsuitable occupations and broadening
Too sparse a k-point mesh for the occupation treatment
Numerical-library, build, or eigensolver failure
inspect: Cell, coordinates, short distances, electron count, and charge
Band count, final-state occupations, broadening, and k-point mesh
Pseudopotential or dataset provenance and warnings
Whether the same failure reproduces with another supported build or solver
safe_next_action: Correct the structure, state, band coverage, occupations, or sampling first.
Use a documented robust eigensolver only as a controlled diagnostic after the input objects are defensible.
preserve_before_retry: The exact error with its preceding output context and complete input
Pseudopotential or dataset hashes and executable, library, and build identities
records.do_not_conclude: Making an eigensolver finish does not prove that the converged electronic state is the intended state or the lowest relevant state.

records.title: A restart or parent artifact cannot be read or trusted
records.symptom: The program cannot recover a calculation, rejects a restart, or a downstream task cannot find or read the expected density, wavefunction, save tree, or response artifact.
records.first_check: Bind the artifact to its exact parent path, project or prefix, program version, termination state, representation, and hash before attempting reuse.
cause_classes: Incomplete or corrupt write from a failed parent run
Wrong ancestry, path, project, prefix, or stale artifact
Incompatible software version or Gamma-only versus k-point representation
Concurrent jobs writing the same scratch identity
inspect: Artifact inventory, size, hash, timestamp, and parent output
Project or prefix, scratch directory, version, and sampling representation
Parent termination and solver markers and the downstream reader's exact error
Concurrent jobs or copied files that could have changed the artifact
safe_next_action: Regenerate the artifact from an accepted parent or start from scratch when lineage or integrity cannot be established.
Use restart conversion or reuse only where the official compatibility contract explicitly permits it.
preserve_before_retry: A manifest and hashes of the failing artifact set and its parent output
The failed reader output, exact paths, project or prefix, version, and launch command
records.do_not_conclude: A filename, readable file, or successful restart does not prove correct lineage, parent convergence, or suitability for the downstream observable.

records.title: I/O, memory, MPI, or scratch fails
records.symptom: The run reports an I/O error, segmentation fault, out-of-memory termination, disk or quota failure, or an intermittent parallel or network-filesystem error.
records.first_check: Read the scheduler resource and exit record with standard error, then inspect disk space, quota, permissions, scratch identity, and concurrent writers.
cause_classes: Insufficient memory or stack and an unsuitable parallel decomposition
Disk space, quota, permissions, or network-filesystem failure
MPI, compiler, mathematical-library, or hardware incompatibility
Two jobs sharing a project, prefix, filename, or scratch directory
inspect: Scheduler state, peak memory, exit code, and node-level error messages
Free space, quota, permissions, ownership, and scratch location
MPI and library versions, process layout, and reproducibility across supported environments
Concurrent processes, repeated project identities, and partial files
safe_next_action: Correct the demonstrated resource, storage, parallel, or environment fault and give every run an isolated scratch identity.
Do not continue from an artifact whose write integrity is uncertain.
preserve_before_retry: Job ID, command, resource request, standard output, standard error, and host/software identity
Scratch inventory, relevant file hashes, ownership, and the observed resource or storage limit
records.do_not_conclude: An infrastructure or I/O failure is not physical instability, numerical evidence for a material, or a scientifically meaningful negative result.

records.title: The geometry optimization stalls or exits without an acceptable structure
records.symptom: The optimizer reports an error, reaches its step limit, repeats large moves, or exits without satisfying the active force and stress conditions.
records.first_check: Verify electronic convergence at every ionic step, then inspect every free force component, relevant stress component, displacement, constraint, and electronic-state identity.
cause_classes: Noisy forces caused by insufficient electronic or numerical convergence
Poor initial geometry, close contacts, or an unintended electronic state
Incorrect constraints, relaxed degrees of freedom, or cell objective
Floppy modes, excessive ionic steps, or inconsistent energy and force quality
inspect: The final complete force block and every active constraint
Relevant stress components, geometry trajectory, step sizes, and objective history
Electronic convergence and state identity at each ionic step
Initial and final geometries, symmetry changes, and numerical settings that control force quality
safe_next_action: Run a fresh fixed-geometry electronic evaluation on the exact final coordinates and audit its forces, stress, and state.
Correct force-quality, geometry, or degree-of-freedom problems before making one bounded optimizer or step-control change.
preserve_before_retry: The complete trajectory, initial and final structures, constraints, and active degrees of freedom
All inputs and outputs needed to bind force, stress, electronic state, and restart ancestry
records.do_not_conclude: Optimizer completion does not establish a global minimum, the lowest relevant electronic state, dynamical stability, or target-observable convergence.

records.title: Detected symmetry or k/q mapping differs from the intended model
records.symptom: The code finds fewer operations than expected, changes the irreducible mesh, reports a q-point star or degeneracy error, or identifies a different primitive-cell relation.
records.first_check: Compare the exact cell, fractional coordinates, coordinate precision, and magnetic state with the operations reported by the code and with the declared computational model.
cause_classes: Rounded coordinates, a rotated cell, or sites only approximately related by symmetry
Primitive-versus-conventional-cell or supercell ambiguity
A q point near but not exactly at the intended high-symmetry position
Fractional translations, FFT-grid compatibility, or magnetic symmetry
inspect: Cell matrix, fractional coordinates, significant figures, species, and magnetic order
Reported operations, primitive-cell relation, and irreducible k- or q-point sets
The exact structure transformation and symmetry tolerance used before the run
Whether cutoff or cell changes altered an automatically selected real-space grid
safe_next_action: Correct or standardize the intentional model and regenerate every dependent k mesh, q mesh, and path.
Do not disable symmetry merely to suppress a diagnostic without explaining the model change.
preserve_before_retry: Source and transformed structures, transformation record, tolerance, and software version
Before-and-after symmetry reports and all dependent sampling definitions
records.do_not_conclude: A changed symmetry count alone does not establish a phase transition, broken physics, or a software defect.

records.title: The harmonic phonon calculation contains imaginary frequencies
records.symptom: One or more dynamical-matrix eigenvalues are negative, corresponding to imaginary phonon frequencies; some outputs or plots show these frequencies with a negative sign at Gamma or another q point.
records.first_check: Classify acoustic and non-acoustic modes, q point, magnitude, and eigenvector, then audit the parent geometry, residual forces and stress, electronic convergence, and response convergence.
cause_classes: Acoustic-sum-rule violation, interpolation artifact, or numerical noise
Residual force, stress, or an insufficiently converged electronic parent
Insufficient cutoff, k mesh, q mesh, supercell, or force-constant range
Incorrect masses or data, or a genuine instability of the chosen structure
inspect: Frequencies, eigenvectors, q-point identity, degeneracy, and whether the mode is acoustic
Parent forces, stress, structure, electronic thresholds, and response thresholds
k/q commensurability, q ledger or supercell, interpolation, masses, and non-analytic treatment
Mode-displaced structures and convergence of the mode under controlled numerical changes
safe_next_action: Use an acoustic sum rule only as a diagnostic, then converge the parent state, response, and sampling and inspect the eigenvector.
Recalculate on the accepted structure before following a mode or making a physical stability claim.
preserve_before_retry: Parent and phonon inputs and outputs, dynamical matrices or force constants, and q-point ledger
Mode eigenvectors, raw frequencies, interpolation settings, software version, and convergence series
records.do_not_conclude: An imaginary frequency alone does not prove a physical instability. Removing it with an acoustic sum rule or a single parameter change does not validate the phonon calculation or establish full-zone dynamical stability.
